## Plain Language Summary and Project Impact

On aarch64 a load/store-exclusive retry loop retires a variable number of branches for the same
work. Any exception between the pair clears the local exclusive monitor, the store-exclusive
fails, and the loop runs again: a timer tick, an IPI, a page fault, a PMU overflow, a ptrace stop.
Hermit counts retired branches to place preemptions and to replay a schedule, so a program built
with those loops cannot be replayed exactly on aarch64. The programs that matter here are the ones
nobody can rebuild: a prebuilt sanitizer runtime, a system libc, a service shipped on a device.

`hermit run --rewrite-exclusives` rewrites each canonical exclusive loop in the guest executable,
and in any file named by `--rewrite-exclusives-also`, into a single FEAT_LSE atomic instruction,
and bind-mounts the rewritten copy over the path the guest loads it from. Only code the file
proves is rewritten: what its ARM mapping symbols mark `$x`. A stripped file, or a section that
holds a mapping symbol other than `$x` and `$d`, is left unchanged and named
(`no-mapping-symbols`, `unsupported-mapping-symbol`). `--rewrite-exclusives-stripped=heuristic`
is an explicit opt-in that rewrites stripped files by a stripped-file heuristic whose residuals
are documented, including that a mistaken classification can corrupt program data. `hermit
rewrite-exclusives FILE...` reports the same analysis without running anything, so an image can be
inspected before anyone runs it, and exits nonzero when a file still holds a loop it refused or a
section it skipped.

Before: a four-thread atomic-counter program built with exclusive loops diverged in all four
`--strict --verify --verify-strict` runs, and a multi-process sanitizer test's recorded schedule
could not be replayed at all. After: the same program reaches bitwise parity in all four, and the
same test's schedule replays byte-identically in all four seeds, including reproducing the failure
the recording caught.

This is binary rewriting used as preprocessing for the ptrace backend, in the same sense as
e9patch (`docs/E9PATCH_COMPATIBILITY.md`). It loads no Detcore tool through Reverie and is not a
backend. It is refused on every other backend.

## Mechanism

Four idioms are recognised, each a contiguous window that ends in `CBNZ Rs, <loop top>`:

| Idiom | Original | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| Rmw | `LDxXR Rt; <alu> Rd,Rt,op; STxXR Rs,Rd; CBNZ Rs` | materialise the operand in Rs; `LD<op>`; the original ALU instruction; `MOV Ws,WZR` |
| Swap | `LDxXR Rt; STxXR Rs,Rv; CBNZ Rs` | `SWP Rv,Rt,[Rn]`; `MOV Ws,WZR`; `NOP` |
| CasCompare | `LDxXR Rt; CMP Rt,X; B.NE out; STxXR Rs,Rv; CBNZ Rs` | `MOV Rt,X`; `CAS Rt,Rv,[Rn]`; the original CMP; the original B.NE, re-encoded one slot later; `MOV Ws,WZR` |
| CasZero | `LDxXR Rt; CBNZ Rt,out; STxXR Rs,Rv; CBNZ Rs` | `MOV Rt,ZR`; `CAS Rt,Rv,[Rn]`; the CBNZ re-encoded one slot later; `MOV Ws,WZR` |

The replacement is the same length and in place, so every instruction keeps its address: every
PC-relative branch, return address, unwind table entry, symbol and signal PC stays valid, and no
trampoline or scratch page is needed.

The scratch registers are the loop's own. A retry loop writes its status register unconditionally
before anything can read it, and its load destination likewise, so neither holds a live value at
the loop's entry; the replacement uses them to materialise its operand and restores on every exit
path exactly the value the original left there. The status register may also BE the load
destination, which is what LLVM emits for a compare-and-swap; the compare-and-swap replacements
handle that case and the read-modify-write one refuses it, because an atomic with one register in
both the operand and destination roles is CONSTRAINED UNPREDICTABLE.

Anything that is not a fully decoded canonical loop is left exactly as it was and reported with
its address and a reason: an exclusive pair instruction, no paired load, an instruction in the
window outside the decoded subset, a non-canonical shape, a direct branch from elsewhere into the
middle of the sequence, a register constraint the replacement needs, an operation with no
single-instruction LSE form, or a moved branch that would no longer reach its target.

Only sections marked `SHF_EXECINSTR` are scanned. An executable `PT_LOAD` segment also carries the
ELF header, the dynamic symbol and relocation tables and read-only data, and those bytes decode as
instructions as readily as code does: on one Android test binary a segment scan reported 69
exclusive instructions where `.text` holds 6. A file with no section headers is left alone and
said to be, and a section in a writable executable mapping is skipped rather than rewritten.

Within those sections only code is rewritten, and by default only what ARM mapping symbols prove
is code. The AArch64 ELF ABI has the assembler place a local, untyped mapping symbol at every
switch between code (`$x`) and data (`$d`). The rewriter takes exactly the `$x` ranges, `$d` wins
a tie, and a sequence that a literal load or `ADR` in the code reaches is refused. A section that
no mapping symbol marks, as in every stripped file, is not read for code: each sequence in it is
left alone as `no-mapping-symbols`. A section that holds a mapping symbol other than `$x` and `$d`
(AArch32's `$a` or `$t`, or an unknown `$` name) is not proved by its marks, and under either
policy each sequence in it is refused as `unsupported-mapping-symbol`, naming the symbol. Either
way the run prints the file and lists it in its summary (`exclusive_rewrite_unmarked`), and
`hermit rewrite-exclusives --list-refusals` lists each such loop by address.

`--rewrite-exclusives-stripped=heuristic` (`--stripped=heuristic` on `hermit rewrite-exclusives`)
is an explicit opt-in for files without mapping symbols. It takes for code what control reaches
from the entries of the functions the unwind table describes, less what the code or the image
addresses as data. Its residuals, each data that nothing in the image points at, taken for code,
are these: data after a call to an imported function that never returns and whose name it does
not know; what the code addresses after a write that loses an `ADRP`'s carried base; what an
unresolved `ADRP`'s completion reaches past its page; the tail of a table that a false branch
cuts; the bytes after a call to a function that returns through a changed `X30` or a syscall;
and the bytes after a call through `BLR`, whose callee is unknown. A mistaken classification can
corrupt program data. A run under the heuristic says so in its summary
(`exclusive_rewrite_stripped_heuristic`) and in the preemption record it writes, and a replay or
an analysis under the other setting is refused by the record's mark. Under the heuristic,
`--verify-json` and `--verify-run`, the verification exports another tool reads without the
command line, are refused.

## Determinism

The rewritten program cannot retry at the sites that were rewritten, because a single atomic
instruction has no retry: an interrupted atomic is restarted by the kernel at its own instruction
and performs one access. That is the whole mechanism; nothing about it depends on timing. The
report says how many exclusive instructions remain, and a file whose report says zero cannot have
an interrupt-dependent branch count from this cause at all.

The rewrite itself is a pure function of the input bytes and the stripped-file policy: it reads
only the file. Each cached copy is named by the rewriter's format, the policy, a digest of the
rewritten bytes and the source's mode. So the two runs of one `--verify` pair, and a replay of a
recording, map byte-identical images, and runs that would map different bytes (a default run and
a heuristic run of one stripped file) never share a copy. A copy is never written in place: it is
written to a private per-user directory under a temporary name and renamed into place, so a
concurrent writer cannot be observed half-written, and a run that mounted a copy keeps it whatever
another run writes later.

Ordering is carried across pair to atomic, exactly:

| load | store | atomic |
|---|---|---|
| LDAXR | STLXR | `AL` |
| LDAXR | STXR | `A` |
| LDXR | STLXR | `L` |
| LDXR | STXR | plain |

Only register-only instructions are allowed between the pair, so the acquire taken at the atomic
rather than at the load, and the release taken at the atomic rather than at the store, order the
same memory accesses in the same directions. One case is strictly stronger rather than equal: a
`CASAL` whose comparison fails keeps its release semantics, where the original never executed its
`STLXR` at all. More ordering cannot produce an execution the original could not have produced, so
it cannot break a program; it can hide a weak-memory race from a native run, which is one reason
this is opt-in. Under Detcore's sequentialized threads it is unobservable.

## Linux Semantics

No syscall result, errno, signal delivery, or `/proc` or `/sys` content is emulated differently
by this change: it adds no syscall handling and touches no Detcore path. The guest keeps the
same path for its executable, because the rewritten copy is bind-mounted over it, so argv,
`/proc/self/exe` and the executable's path in `/proc/self/maps` are what they were, as for the
e9patch preprocessor that uses the same overlay.

What a guest CAN observe, and what this flag therefore promises:

- It reads its own rewritten instructions. A program that checksums its text, or disassembles
  it, sees the rewrite. The bind mount keeps the path, not the content.
- The file behind that path is the cached copy, so its device, inode, size and timestamps are
  the cache's, and the overlay appears in `/proc/self/mountinfo`.
- A fault inside a rewritten sequence reports a PC one instruction later than the original's
  would, with the materialising `MOV` already executed, because the atomic sits where the
  load-exclusive did. A guest that handles SIGSEGV or SIGBUS and inspects the faulting PC or
  the register state can tell.
- With FEAT_LSE2, which Neoverse V2 has, a misaligned atomic within a 16-byte granule succeeds
  where `LDAXR` would have raised an alignment fault, so a guest that relies on that SIGBUS
  loses it.
- A failed compare-and-swap still takes the write permission check that the never-executed
  store-exclusive would not have taken, so a read-only mapping faults where the original
  returned.

None of these appears in the measured cases, and all of them are reasons the rewrite is opt-in
rather than the default.

The instruction semantics the rewrite relies on are architectural, not kernel behaviour: the
exclusive monitor and its clearing on an exception, and the FEAT_LSE atomic instructions, are
specified in the Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile (DDI 0487, issue L.a), sections
B2.9 "Synchronization and semaphores" (exclusive monitors, and the events that clear them),
C3.2.6 "Load-Exclusive and Store-Exclusive", and C3.2.12 "Atomic instructions". That a compiler
treats the two forms as the same source-level atomic is observable: the same source built
`-march=armv8-a -mno-outline-atomics` and `-march=armv8.1-a` gives the exclusive loop and the
single atomic this rewrite maps between.

## Validation

Host: an NVIDIA Grace (Neoverse V2) server, Linux 6.16, 64 KiB pages. Backend: ptrace. Log level:
default. Relaxations: none, except where a line says otherwise.

- `cargo test -p hermit-run --lib aarch64_lse`: 14 tests, 14 passed, 0 failed, on x86_64, plus
  `cargo test -p hermit-run --bin hermit retained_in_reproducers`, 2 passed;
  `cargo clippy -p hermit-run --lib --bins` and `cargo fmt` clean. The
  module is pure and its tests are target-independent. Every expected encoding in the test table
  is GNU as's own output for the sequence it claims, generated on the aarch64 host rather than
  computed by hand: 14 rewrite cases (four orderings, byte and halfword sizes, both compilers'
  CAS shapes, the LLVM shape whose status register is its load destination, an immediate the
  instruction shifts left by 12, and a sub-word compare a zero extension admits), 6 refusals,
  both zero-register forms, the negative case of each new family, a branch into the middle of a
  sequence, and a loop found at an offset inside a larger region. The tests also assert that a
  rewritten sequence contains no exclusive instruction, and the packed-relative-relocation
  decoder has a case of its own over an address entry and a bitmap entry.
- The `test.hermit_unit` node's pin moves 1102 -> 1117 and `ci/dag/validate.json` is
  regenerated; `generate-validation-dag --check` reports it canonical and fresh. The number is
  derived with that node's own selection: 1123 listed, five removed by its skip patterns and
  one `#[ignore]` test listed but never executed, which is the old pin plus this change's
  fifteen tests.
- L2, exclusive-loop guest (four threads, atomic add and xor, built `-march=armv8-a
  -mno-outline-atomics`): `hermit run --strict --chaos --preemption-timeout=20000 --seed=N
  --epoch=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --verify --verify-strict --verify-json=J`, seeds 1-4. Without the
  flag: `bitwise_parity: false`, diverged 4/4. With it: `bitwise_parity: true`, verdict `matched`,
  4/4, 889-909 compared INFO messages per run. Guest output identical either way.
- Schedule replay, a multi-process sanitizer test (its prebuilt sanitizer runtime carries 461
  exclusive loops): record with `--record-preemptions-to`, then replay with
  `--replay-preemptions-from`, six seeds, chaos, non-strict. Without the flag: **0 of 6**
  replayed. One panicked with `Cannot set RCB end of timeslice to 117460 ... current RCB count is
  already 117646`, the retried branches themselves, and five with the virtual-time form of the
  same overrun, since virtual time advances with retired branches. With the flag: **6 of 6**
  replayed, byte-identical stdout and the recording's outcome, including the test failure the
  recording caught. Measured honestly rather than claimed: in an earlier round one of those seeds
  replayed with a virtual-time overrun WITH the flag on, and identically in the rounds either
  side, so this removes the retried-branch cause of a replay divergence and does not claim to fix
  schedule replay in general. This measurement ran on an integration tree, because two unrelated
  fixes it needs on this host (a pipe-capacity pin for 64 KiB pages, and received-descriptor
  aliasing) are not on main; the rewriter commits are identical in both trees.
- Native differential semantics, no Hermit: 14 workloads covering every idiom and both compilers'
  shapes, each rewritten and run against the original with the same inputs, 3 reps: identical
  results in all 14, and `STREX_FAIL_SPEC` (PMU event 0x6E) reads 0 in the rewritten binaries
  where the originals fail stores under the same load.
- Coverage, by `hermit rewrite-exclusives`: the sanitizer test's LL/SC build 450 of 461 loops
  rewritten (11 left alone: 7 non-canonical, 3 register constraints, 1 shifted subtraction); a
  prebuilt compiler-rt sanitizer runtime 564 of 578; a device's `libc.so` 23 of 23 with nothing
  left and its dynamic linker 33 of 41; a system glibc 2.34 19 of 19; two smaller test cases 4
  of 4 each.
- What the rewrite leaves behind, executed rather than counted: the rewritten sanitizer test
  retires 30 store-exclusives per run against 1,831,781 before it, and the rewritten sanitizer
  harness retires none at all against 250,485. A device's outline-atomics helpers, which are
  where its libc keeps its exclusive loops, are behind a run-time FEAT_LSE check and never
  execute their LL/SC tail on a core that has it.
- The counter this rewrite makes unnecessary was measured on both targets, by a companion study
  on the same branch's evidence: `BR_RETIRED` is an exact linear function of `STREX_FAIL_SPEC`
  on a Neoverse V2 and on a Cortex-A78 (k = 1 for read-modify-write, swap, pair and spinlock
  loops, k = 2 for every compare-and-swap form, residual 0 over 40 repetitions each), and on the
  A78 the other two events this study used, `STREX_SPEC` and `INST_RETIRED`, are accepted by the
  PMU and never scheduled. So a detector built on this must use `BR_RETIRED` and
  `STREX_FAIL_SPEC` alone. No detector code is in this change.
- Not claimed: no run of the full workspace test suite on aarch64, no L3 or L4, no measurement
  under an emulated PMU, and no claim about any backend other than ptrace.

## Human Review Required

Trigger 3: a new determinization strategy. Hermit has not rewritten guest instructions to remove a
source of nondeterminism before; e9patch preprocessing inserts trampolines for instrumentation,
and this replaces one instruction sequence with an architecturally equivalent one so that the
retired-branch count of a given piece of guest work becomes a property of the program alone. The
specific judgements a human should weigh: that the four replacements restore every register and
flag on every exit path, that the pair-to-atomic ordering map is exact (and that the one strictly
stronger case, a failed `CASAL`, is acceptable), and that rewriting a prebuilt image by default is
a decision to take separately from offering it behind a flag.

## Revision: analyze and bisect trials apply the rewrite

Additional commit f2997181e0da95477bf9ffeddd15da9bc87d33ba (tree ab934616), on b1db8a02e. Owner of this commit: vmakaev-metamate (agentcloud, devvm53386); the rest of the pull request is unchanged.

`hermit analyze` and `hermit bisect` accepted `--rewrite-exclusives` in their run arguments and printed it in every trial's reproducer, but no trial applied it. Trials start through `RunOpts::run`, and only `RunOpts::main` prepared the rewritten images. Each trial now prepares them before it starts (`RunOpts::prepare_trial_preprocessing`, called from the trial launch). The overlays are prepared once per process and reused, keyed by everything the preparation reads: program, `--rewrite-exclusives-also` files, backend, mounts and binds, working directory and `PATH`. That gives one rewrite and one report per analysis.

This matters on aarch64. analyze's stack-trace replays stop at every timeslice end, and a single step clears the exclusive monitor, so an unrewritten `LDXR`/`STXR` loop livelocks under single-stepping and the replay desyncs. The Reverie-side fix, stepping over exclusive sequences as one unit, is filed separately; the rewrite is the workaround until then.

Validation (ptrace backend, default log level, relaxations none):
- Intel Xeon host: new CLI test `analyze_trials_prepare_the_exclusive_rewrite_their_reproducer_names` passes. `hermit run --rewrite-exclusives` refuses there (no FEAT_LSE), and the analysis's first trial must refuse the same way. At b1db8a02e the same analysis ran its trials unrewritten and failed elsewhere ("baseline run matched target criteria"). `cargo clippy -p hermit-run --bin hermit --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Grace (Neoverse V2), with this commit (exact tree) on an aarch64 integration build. Case: a FrameRetireHandler hang reproducer whose system ld.so and libc carry 4 and 19 exclusive loops, rewritten with `--rewrite-exclusives-also`. Run: `hermit analyze --prefix-search --run1-seed 1 --target-stderr FRH_HANG -- --strict --chaos --preemption-timeout=1000 --rewrite-exclusives --rewrite-exclusives-also=/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 --rewrite-exclusives-also=/lib64/libc.so.6 -- ./race_nofix`.
  - Result: decision at #7712 in 197 s, 0 desync lines in any trial or stack-trace replay, and the rewrite report printed once.
  - stack1 is thread 5 in `clock_gettime` from `main` race.cpp:26. stack2 is thread 3 in `nanosleep`/`usleep` from `main` race.cpp:27. `racing_accesses` is `timing` and names the two calls.
  - Without this commit, the target run's checkpoints showed the unrewritten ld.so (the first `set_tid_address` at 14,249 retired branches instead of 14,247). Both stack-trace replays desynced (3,262 desync lines) and timed out, stack2 was missing and `racing_accesses` was unavailable.
- hermit-cli's integration tests do not build on aarch64 at this base (`reverie-inguest` is x86-only), so the aarch64 evidence is the measurement above.

**Visibility of the opt-in.**
- **Run summary:** `Config::rewrite_exclusives_stripped_heuristic` is set by the CLI and has no legacy backend key. It becomes `RunSummary::exclusive_rewrite_stripped_heuristic` (JSON, plus an INFO line).
- **Preemption record:** the scheduler stamps it as `rewrite_exclusives_stripped_heuristic`, written only when on.
- **Replay:** a replay (`--replay-preemptions-from`, `--replay-schedule-from`) under the other setting is refused by the record's own mark, as a PolicyRefusal before launch.
- **Analyze and bisect:** trials take the setting from their run arguments, every record analyze writes is stamped with it, recordings made under the other setting are refused before any trial, and the trial-preparation key includes the policy.
- **Verification exports:** the heuristic refuses `--verify-json` and `--verify-run`. These are the two verification exports another tool reads without this command line: the typed report, and the saved run directory that `hermit log-diff --verify-json` compares. Neither would show the heuristic. The refusal sits in `main_with_backend`, before dispatch, and again in `prepare_exclusive_rewrite`, so analyze trials and library callers hit it too. Plain `--verify` stays allowed, because its verdict is printed beside the run's own summary, which states the heuristic.
